source: IPEC (2016) Core Competencies for Interprofessional Collaborative Practice

domains.name: Values and Ethics for Interprofessional Practice
domains.description: Work with individuals of other professions to maintain a climate of mutual respect and shared values

sub_competencies.title: Place interests of patients and populations at center of interprofessional health care delivery
Respect the dignity and privacy of patients while maintaining confidentiality
Embrace cultural diversity and individual differences
Respect the unique cultures, values, roles/responsibilities of other health professions
Work with individuals of other professions to maintain mutual respect and shared values
Develop a trusting relationship with patients, families, and other team members
Demonstrate high standards of ethical conduct in contributions to others
Manage ethical dilemmas specific to interprofessional practice
Act with honesty and integrity in relationships with patients, families, and team members
Maintain competence in own profession appropriate to scope of practice

domains.name: Roles and Responsibilities
domains.description: Use the knowledge of one's own role and those of other professions to appropriately assess and address health care needs of patients

sub_competencies.title: Communicate one's roles and responsibilities clearly to patients, families, and professionals
Recognize one's limitations in skills, knowledge, and abilities
Engage diverse professionals who complement one's own expertise to optimize care
Explain the roles and responsibilities of other care providers
Use the full scope of knowledge, skills, and abilities of professionals from health to provide care
Communicate with team members to clarify each member's responsibility in executing care plan
Forge interdependent relationships with other professions to improve care and advance learning
Engage in continuous professional and interprofessional development
Use unique and complementary abilities of all members of the team to optimize care
Describe how professionals in health and other fields can collaborate and integrate

domains.name: Interprofessional Communication
domains.description: Communicate with patients, families, communities, and professionals in health and other fields in a responsive and responsible manner

sub_competencies.title: Choose effective communication tools and techniques for interprofessional interactions
Communicate information with patients, families, and team members in an understandable form
Express one's knowledge and opinions to team members with confidence, clarity, and respect
Listen actively and encourage ideas and opinions of other team members
Give timely, sensitive, instructive feedback to others about their performance
Use respectful language appropriate for a given difficult situation, conflict, or disagreement
Recognize how one's uniqueness contributes to effective communication and conflict resolution
Communicate consistently the importance of teamwork in patient-centered care

domains.name: Teams and Teamwork
domains.description: Apply relationship-building values and principles of team dynamics to perform effectively in different team roles

sub_competencies.title: Describe the process of team development and the roles and practices of effective teams
Develop consensus on the ethical principles to guide all aspects of team work
Engage health and other professionals in shared patient-centered and population-focused problem-solving
Integrate the knowledge and experience of other professions to inform health care decisions
Apply leadership practices that support collaborative practice and team effectiveness
Engage self and others to constructively manage disagreements about values, roles, goals, and actions
Share accountability with other professions, patients, and communities for outcomes relevant to prevention and health care
Reflect on individual and team performance for individual and team performance improvement
Use process improvement strategies to increase the effectiveness of interprofessional teamwork
Use available evidence to inform effective teamwork and team-based practices
